question: What is the minimum age to apply for an instruction permit if you are enrolling in a driver training course?
correctAnswer: 15 years old
explanation: If you are enrolling in a driver training course, you can apply for your instruction permit as early as 15 years old.

question: If you are NOT enrolling in a driver training course, at what age can you take the knowledge exam?
correctAnswer: 15½ years old
explanation: If you are not enrolling in a driver training course, you can take the knowledge exam after you turn 15½.

question: How long is a Washington instruction permit valid?
correctAnswer: 1 year
explanation: Your instruction permit is valid for 1 year and can be renewed for a fee.

question: How long is your knowledge exam score valid after you pass?
correctAnswer: 2 years
explanation: Your knowledge exam score is valid for 2 years. If you wait too long to take your skills exam, you may have to take the knowledge exam again.

question: How long must you hold your instruction permit before getting your first driver license (ages 16–17)?
correctAnswer: 6 months
explanation: To get your first driver license at ages 16–17, you must have your instruction permit for at least 6 months.

question: What is the minimum age to get your first driver license in Washington?
correctAnswer: 16 years old
explanation: You must be at least 16 years old and a Washington resident to get your first driver license.

question: How many hours of supervised day driving are required before getting your first license (ages 16–17)?
correctAnswer: 40 hours
explanation: You must complete at least 40 hours of day driving and 10 hours of night driving with a licensed driver who has 3 or more years of experience.

question: How many hours of supervised night driving are required before getting your first license (ages 16–17)?
correctAnswer: 10 hours
explanation: You must complete at least 10 hours of night driving with a licensed driver who has 3 or more years of experience.

question: Your supervising driver must have at least how many years of driving experience (for applicants ages 16–17)?
correctAnswer: 3 years
explanation: Practice driving must be done with a licensed driver who has 3 or more years of experience.

question: During the first 6 months of an intermediate driver license, who may ride as passengers?
optionA: No more than 3 passengers under age 20
optionC: Only one passenger of any age
optionD: No passengers under age 20 except immediate family members
correctAnswer: No passengers under age 20 except immediate family members
explanation: During the first 6 months of an intermediate license, no passengers under age 20 are allowed except immediate family members.

question: After the first 6 months of an intermediate driver license, how many passengers under age 20 are allowed (besides immediate family)?
correctAnswer: 3 passengers
explanation: From 6 months to age 18 (or one year, whichever comes first), no more than 3 passengers under age 20 are allowed except immediate family members.

question: During the first 6 months of an intermediate license, what are the nighttime driving restrictions?
optionA: No driving between midnight and 6 a.m.
optionB: No driving between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m.
optionC: No driving between 1 a.m. and 5 a.m. unless accompanied by a parent, guardian, or licensed driver at least age 25
correctAnswer: No driving between 1 a.m. and 5 a.m. unless accompanied by a parent, guardian, or licensed driver at least age 25
explanation: Intermediate license holders cannot drive between 1 a.m. and 5 a.m. unless accompanied by a parent, guardian, or licensed driver at least age 25.

question: When are the nighttime restrictions on an intermediate driver license lifted?
optionA: After 6 months regardless of driving record
optionC: After one year of safe driving
optionD: After completing an additional driver education course
correctAnswer: After one year of safe driving
explanation: Nighttime restrictions expire after one year of safe driving — meaning no crashes or traffic offenses.

question: What is the penalty for a second traffic violation while holding an intermediate driver license?
optionB: Current restrictions remain until you turn 18
optionC: License is suspended for 6 months or until you turn 18, whichever comes first
correctAnswer: License is suspended for 6 months or until you turn 18, whichever comes first
explanation: For a second violation, the intermediate license is suspended for 6 months or until the driver turns 18, whichever comes first.

question: What happens to intermediate license restrictions when you turn 18?
optionA: You must visit a licensing office to have them removed
optionB: You must pass an additional exam
optionD: You must apply for a new unrestricted license
correctAnswer: Restrictions are automatically lifted
explanation: You don't need to get a new license when you turn 18. Intermediate driver license restrictions are automatically lifted.

question: How many days do new residents (age 18+) with a valid out-of-state license have to obtain a Washington driver license?
correctAnswer: 30 days
explanation: New residents who are licensed in another state have 30 days to obtain a Washington State driver license.

question: Within how many days must you update your address in License Express after moving?
correctAnswer: 10 days
explanation: If your address changes, you must update your information in License Express within 10 days of the change.

question: Where must name changes be made?
optionC: By mailing a form to DOL
correctAnswer: At a driver licensing office
explanation: Name changes must be made in person at a driver licensing office; they cannot be done online.

question: What does REAL ID refer to?
optionA: A federal law, not an actual piece of ID
optionB: A specific type of identification card
correctAnswer: A federal law, not an actual piece of ID
explanation: REAL ID is a law, not an actual piece of ID. An enhanced driver license is among several options that meet REAL ID requirements.

question: Which type of Washington ID can be used for international border crossings by land or sea?
correctAnswer: Enhanced driver license or ID
explanation: An enhanced driver license or ID can be used for international border crossing by land or sea to Canada, Mexico, and the Caribbean.

question: How long is the temporary license you receive at the licensing office valid?
correctAnswer: 45 days
explanation: Before leaving the licensing office, you receive a temporary license that is good for 45 days. Your official license will be mailed to you.

question: If you are 18 or older and want to practice driving with a licensed driver before taking the skills exam, your supervising driver must have at least how many years of experience?
correctAnswer: 5 years
explanation: For drivers 18+, one option is to get a permit and practice driving with a licensed driver who has 5 or more years of experience before taking the skills exam.

question: If your driver license has been expired for 8 or more years, what must you do to renew it?
optionA: Pay an additional late fee only
optionB: Retake the knowledge and skills exams
optionD: Provide a letter from your insurance company
correctAnswer: Retake the knowledge and skills exams
explanation: If your license is 8 or more years expired, you'll need to retake the skills and knowledge exams.

question: Can you use a cell phone with hands-free technology while driving with an intermediate license?
optionA: Yes, hands-free devices are always allowed
optionB: No, except to report an emergency
optionC: Yes, but only for navigation purposes
optionD: No, phones must be turned off completely
correctAnswer: No, except to report an emergency
explanation: Intermediate license laws restrict the use of cell phones and wireless communication devices while driving, even with hands-free technology. You can only use your phone to report an emergency.

question: What is the minimum classroom instruction required for a traffic safety course from another state to meet Washington's requirements?
correctAnswer: 30 hours
explanation: A traffic safety course completed in another state must meet Washington's minimum requirement of 30 hours of classroom and 6 hours of behind-the-wheel instruction.

question: How many hours of behind-the-wheel instruction with a licensed instructor are required at a minimum for a traffic safety course?
correctAnswer: 6 hours
explanation: Washington requires a minimum of 6 hours of behind-the-wheel instruction as part of a traffic safety course.

question: What is the total minimum supervised driving practice required for applicants ages 16–17 (day + night combined)?
correctAnswer: 50 hours
explanation: Applicants must complete at least 40 hours of day driving plus 10 hours of night driving, totaling 50 hours. The parental authorization form certifies you have at least 50 hours of driving experience.

question: Who is allowed in the vehicle during the Driving Skills Exam?
optionA: You, the examiner, and one parent or guardian
optionB: You and the examiner only, with exceptions for service animals and sign language interpreters
optionC: You, the examiner, and your driving instructor
optionD: You and up to two other people approved by the examiner
correctAnswer: You and the examiner only, with exceptions for service animals and sign language interpreters
explanation: Only you and the examiner are allowed in the vehicle during the exam. Exceptions are made for service animals and sign language interpreters.

question: For a first-time license applicant ages 16–17, how long must you be free of traffic violations before applying?
correctAnswer: 6 months
explanation: You must be without any traffic violations or convictions for 6 months prior to applying for the license.

question: What exception allows intermediate license holders to drive at any hour and with passengers?
optionA: Having completed an advanced driving course
optionD: Being employed and driving to work
correctAnswer: Driving for agricultural purposes
explanation: Intermediate driver license holders may drive at any hour, with passengers, for agricultural purposes.

question: What is the minimum liability insurance coverage required in Washington for bodily injury or death of one person in a collision?
explanation: Washington requires at least $25,000 payable for bodily injury or death of one person in a collision.

question: What is the minimum liability insurance coverage required in Washington for bodily injury or death of two or more persons in one collision?
explanation: Washington requires at least $50,000 payable for bodily injury or death of two or more persons in any one collision.

question: What is the minimum liability insurance coverage required in Washington for property damage in one collision?
explanation: Washington requires at least $10,000 payable for injury to or destruction of property of others in any one collision.

question: Where must you keep your proof of liability insurance in Washington?
optionA: Only at home in a secure location
optionB: Filed at the Department of Licensing
optionC: Only in a digital format on your phone
optionD: With you or in your vehicle
correctAnswer: With you or in your vehicle
explanation: You must keep proof of insurance with you or in your vehicle at all times.

question: Within how many days must you file a Vehicle Report of Sale after selling your vehicle to another individual?
correctAnswer: 5 days
explanation: If you sell, trade, gift, or dispose of your vehicle, you must file a Vehicle Report of Sale within 5 days.

question: After purchasing a vehicle from an individual, within how many days must the buyer transfer ownership to avoid penalty fees?
correctAnswer: 15 days
explanation: The purchaser must bring the signed title to a licensing office to transfer ownership within 15 days to avoid penalty fees.

question: Does filing a Vehicle Report of Sale transfer ownership of a vehicle?
optionA: Yes, ownership transfers automatically when the report is filed
optionB: No, the title must be signed and given to the purchaser to transfer ownership
optionD: Yes, if both parties sign the report
correctAnswer: No, the title must be signed and given to the purchaser to transfer ownership
explanation: A report of sale does not transfer ownership. The title must be signed and dated by the owner(s) and given to the purchaser, who must then bring it to a licensing office.

question: Where must license plates be displayed on motor vehicles registered in Washington?
correctAnswer: Front and rear
explanation: License plates must be clearly displayed on the front and rear of motor vehicles registered in Washington.

question: What is illegal regarding license plate frames in Washington?
optionA: Using any type of frame around the plate
optionB: Using a colored or decorative frame
optionC: Covering the letters, numbers, or tabs on the plate
optionD: Using a frame not purchased from the dealer
correctAnswer: Covering the letters, numbers, or tabs on the plate
explanation: You can have a license plate frame, but it's illegal to cover the letters, numbers, or tabs on the plate.

question: How many days do new Washington residents have to complete their vehicle registration?
correctAnswer: 30 days
explanation: New residents have 30 days to complete their vehicle registration in Washington.

question: Until what age must children ride in a rear-facing car seat in Washington?
correctAnswer: Age 2
explanation: Children up to age 2 must ride in a rear-facing car seat.

question: At what age range must children ride in a car seat with a rear- or forward-facing harness in Washington?
correctAnswer: 2 to 4 years
explanation: Children ages 2 to 4 years must ride in a car seat with a rear- or forward-facing harness.

question: At what height can a child transition from a booster seat to using just a seat belt in Washington?
correctAnswer: Over 4 feet 9 inches tall
explanation: Children must ride in a car or booster seat until the vehicle lap and shoulder seat belts fit properly, typically when they are over 4'9" tall.

question: Why should children under the age of 13 never ride in the front seat?
optionA: They cannot reach the dashboard controls
optionB: They could be seriously injured or killed if an airbag deploys
optionC: It is illegal for them to wear a seat belt in front
optionD: The front seat offers less legroom for children
correctAnswer: They could be seriously injured or killed if an airbag deploys
explanation: Children under age 13 should never ride in the front seat because they could be seriously injured or killed if an airbag deploys.

question: How far should your chest be from the steering wheel to allow space for the airbag?
correctAnswer: At least 10 inches
explanation: Your chest should be at least 10 inches from the steering wheel to leave space for the airbag.

question: Where should the headrest be positioned to protect against whiplash?
optionB: Even with the top of your head
optionC: At the base of your neck
optionD: Above the top of your head
correctAnswer: Even with your ears
explanation: To protect yourself from whiplash, make sure the headrest is even with your ears.

question: What is the recommended hand position on the steering wheel for most driving situations?
correctAnswer: 9 and 3 o'clock
explanation: Place your hands on the top half of the steering wheel at 9 and 3 (or 10 and 2) for the best control.

question: Which steering method is recommended because it keeps your arms away from the airbag area?
correctAnswer: Hand-to-hand (pull/push) steering
explanation: Hand-to-hand (pull/push) steering keeps both hands on the wheel without crossing over, reducing the chance of arm or hand injury if the airbag deploys.

question: When should you use hand-over-hand steering?
optionA: When turning at low speeds, with limited visibility, or when parking
optionB: Only on highways at high speeds
correctAnswer: When turning at low speeds, with limited visibility, or when parking
explanation: Hand-over-hand steering is used when turning at low speeds, with limited visibility, at an intersection, when parking, or when recovering from a skid.

question: Which hand position is recommended when backing a vehicle using one-hand steering?
correctAnswer: The 12 o'clock position
explanation: The 12 o'clock position is recommended only when backing a vehicle using one-hand steering.

question: What is the primary safety advantage of an Antilock Brake System (ABS)?
optionA: It allows you to steer during emergency braking
optionC: It eliminates the need for brake maintenance
optionD: It automatically stops the vehicle at red lights
correctAnswer: It allows you to steer during emergency braking
explanation: ABS offers an important safety advantage by allowing drivers to steer during an emergency braking situation. It does not shorten stopping distance but allows better steering control.

question: What is a common misconception about ABS that the driver guide corrects?
optionA: ABS eliminates the need for tire tread
optionB: ABS works only at high speeds
correctAnswer: ABS shortens stopping distance
explanation: An ABS does not shorten your stopping distance, but it will allow you to keep better steering control during emergency braking.

question: What happens to a vehicle's weight distribution when you accelerate?
optionA: Weight shifts to the left side
optionB: Weight shifts to the front of the vehicle
optionC: Weight shifts to the back of the vehicle
correctAnswer: Weight shifts to the back of the vehicle
explanation: When you accelerate, the weight of the vehicle shifts to the back and increases pressure on the rear of the vehicle. This is called pitch.

question: What happens to a vehicle's weight distribution when you brake abruptly?
optionA: Weight shifts forward, increasing pressure on the front
optionB: Weight shifts to the back of the vehicle
optionC: Weight shifts equally to both sides
correctAnswer: Weight shifts forward, increasing pressure on the front
explanation: If you stop abruptly, the weight shifts forward, increasing pressure on the front of the vehicle.

question: What is the term for the side-to-side weight shift that occurs when a vehicle turns?
correctAnswer: Roll
explanation: Roll is the side-to-side motion of a vehicle. When you make a turn, centrifugal force transfers weight to the outside of the vehicle, causing the body to roll to one side.

question: When stopped at an intersection, what reference point indicates you are approximately 3 to 6 inches from the stop line?
optionA: The stop line is under your front bumper
optionB: The stop line is at the center of your hood
optionC: The stop line is under your side mirror
optionD: The stop line is visible between your front tires
correctAnswer: The stop line is under your side mirror
explanation: At an intersection, stopping when the stop line is under your side mirror means you are about 3 to 6 inches from the line.

question: How can you determine your approximate lane position while driving?
optionB: Check that the center of your hood is in line with lane markings
optionC: Look at where your tires meet the road
optionD: Follow the vehicle ahead of you
correctAnswer: Check that the center of your hood is in line with lane markings
explanation: To determine your lane position, check that the center of your hood is in line with lane markings. If they're in line, you're approximately 3 to 6 inches from the edge of the lane.

question: What is the best way to tell if you are in a large truck's blind zone (no-zone)?
optionA: If you are within 200 feet of the truck
optionB: If you can hear the truck's engine
optionC: If you are behind the truck's rear axle
optionD: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you
correctAnswer: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you
explanation: If you can't see a large vehicle's mirrors, the driver can't see you. Large vehicles have bigger blind zones called 'no zones.'

question: What should you do if you find yourself in another vehicle's blind zone?
optionA: Honk your horn to alert the other driver
optionC: Speed up or slow down so the driver can see you
optionD: Maintain your position until the other vehicle moves
correctAnswer: Speed up or slow down so the driver can see you
explanation: You need to be aware of other vehicles' blind zones and do your best to stay out of them. You can speed up or slow down so the driver can clearly see you.

question: What is the minimum tire tread depth required for safe driving?
correctAnswer: 2/32 of an inch
explanation: Tire tread shouldn't be less than 2/32 of an inch. Worn tires can cause slipping and sliding, especially on wet roads.

question: You must switch from high beams to regular headlights when you are within what distance of an oncoming vehicle?
correctAnswer: 500 feet
explanation: You must switch back to regular headlights when you are 500 feet in front of an oncoming vehicle.

question: When following another vehicle, at what distance must you switch from high beams to regular headlights?
correctAnswer: 300 feet
explanation: You must switch back to regular headlights when you are 300 feet behind another vehicle.

question: From what distance must brake lights be clearly visible?
correctAnswer: 100 feet
explanation: Your brake lights are red and must be clearly visible from 100 feet away.

question: How far in advance should you signal before making a turn?
correctAnswer: 100 feet
explanation: You should signal 100 feet before you make your move when turning.

question: Which of the following is part of the recommended pre-drive checklist?
optionB: Warm up the engine for 10 minutes
optionC: Check for fluid leaks under the vehicle and obstructions around it
optionD: Check tire pressure with a gauge before every trip
correctAnswer: Check for fluid leaks under the vehicle and obstructions around it
explanation: Before driving, check outside your vehicle for foreign objects in tires, broken glass, fluid leaks, obstructions, children, pets, or weather-related obstacles.

question: In Washington, what is the legal BAC (blood alcohol concentration) limit for drivers age 21 and older?
explanation: For drivers age 21 and older, having a BAC of 0.08% or higher is considered a DUI and can result in legal consequences.

question: What is the BAC limit for drivers under age 21 in Washington?
explanation: Drivers under age 21 face DUI consequences for having a BAC of 0.02% or more, reflecting Washington's stricter standard for minors.

question: For drivers age 21 and older, what is the legal THC limit in Washington?
correctAnswer: 5 nanograms per milliliter of blood
explanation: For drivers age 21 and older, having more than 5 nanograms of active THC per milliliter of blood is considered a DUI.

question: What is the THC limit for drivers under age 21 in Washington?
optionD: Anything above 0 nanograms per milliliter of blood
correctAnswer: Anything above 0 nanograms per milliliter of blood
explanation: Drivers under age 21 face DUI consequences for anything more than 0 nanograms of active THC per milliliter of blood in their system.

question: Under Washington's Implied Consent Law, what do you agree to when you drive in the state?
optionA: You agree to carry proof of insurance at all times
optionB: You agree to pull over for any law enforcement request
optionC: You agree to submit to a vehicle inspection at any time
optionD: You agree to be tested if an officer suspects you are under the influence of alcohol or drugs
correctAnswer: You agree to be tested if an officer suspects you are under the influence of alcohol or drugs
explanation: Under the Implied Consent Law (RCW 46.20.308), everyone who drives in Washington agrees to be tested if an officer suspects they are under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

question: If you refuse to submit to a BAC or drug test in Washington, how long could you lose your driving privilege?
correctAnswer: 90 to 730 days
explanation: If you refuse to be tested, you could lose your driving privilege for 90 to 730 days, or until you reach age 21, whichever is longer.

question: A 19-year-old driver refuses a breath test after being pulled over on suspicion of DUI. What is the minimum period they could lose their driving privilege?
optionD: The longer of 90 days or until they reach age 21
correctAnswer: The longer of 90 days or until they reach age 21
explanation: If you refuse to be tested, you could lose your driving privilege for 90 to 730 days, or until you reach age 21, whichever is longer. For a 19-year-old, reaching age 21 would be longer than 90 days.

question: In Washington, DUI applies to which of the following situations?
optionA: Only when the vehicle is moving on a public road
optionB: Only when the vehicle is moving above 5 mph
optionC: Being in physical control of a vehicle, even if it is parked
optionD: Only when the vehicle is on a highway
correctAnswer: Being in physical control of a vehicle, even if it is parked
explanation: DUI also applies to being in control of a vehicle, even if it's parked. If you have the ability to take control of a vehicle's engine or operation, you are considered in physical control of the vehicle.

question: What is the range of license suspension for a DUI conviction in Washington?
correctAnswer: 90 days to 4 years
explanation: DUI convictions can include driving privileges suspended for 90 days to 4 years, depending on the circumstances and prior offenses.

question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a potential consequence of a DUI conviction in Washington?
optionA: Ignition interlock device required to drive
optionB: Community service of at least 200 hours
optionD: Required alcohol assessment and treatment report
correctAnswer: Community service of at least 200 hours
explanation: DUI convictions can include loss of license, heavy fines, criminal penalties, jail, higher insurance rates, ignition interlock devices, and required alcohol assessment. Community service of 200 hours is not listed in the guide.

question: Under Washington's open container law, where must open alcohol or cannabis products be transported?
optionC: In a trunk or truck bed
optionD: In any sealed bag within the vehicle
correctAnswer: In a trunk or truck bed
explanation: Open alcohol and cannabis products can only be transported in a trunk or truck bed. They cannot be kept in storage compartments accessible to the driver.

question: Which of the following violates Washington's open container law?
optionA: A bottle of alcohol with a broken seal in the passenger area
optionB: A partially consumed bottle of alcohol in the trunk
optionC: An unopened bottle of wine on the back seat
optionD: A sealed six-pack in the back seat
correctAnswer: A bottle of alcohol with a broken seal in the passenger area
explanation: It is a traffic infraction if any person in a vehicle possesses alcohol containers that have been opened, have a broken seal, or are partially consumed in the passenger area. Such items must be in a trunk or truck bed.

question: How long do alcohol- and drug-related offenses remain on your driving record in Washington?
correctAnswer: For life
explanation: Alcohol- and drug-related offenses appear on your driving record for life.

question: Which of the following is an effect of alcohol on driving ability?
optionC: Reduced reaction times and difficulty doing multiple tasks
correctAnswer: Reduced reaction times and difficulty doing multiple tasks
explanation: Alcohol can cause reduced reaction times, concentration, and ability to scan the environment, as well as difficulty doing multiple tasks at once, like staying in a lane and avoiding other traffic.

question: Which psychological effect does alcohol have that makes it particularly dangerous for drivers?
optionA: It causes excessive caution and hesitation
optionB: It causes drivers to drive below the speed limit
optionC: It makes drivers overly aware of other vehicles
optionD: It produces overconfidence, which can lead to risky driving behavior
correctAnswer: It produces overconfidence, which can lead to risky driving behavior
explanation: Alcohol can cause overconfidence, which can lead to risky driving behavior. This is especially dangerous because impaired drivers may believe they are driving safely when they are not.

question: In Washington, recreational use of marijuana is legal for those age 21 and over. When is it legal to drive after consuming cannabis?
optionA: Driving after consuming any cannabis is illegal for all ages
optionB: When you feel the effects have worn off
optionC: When your THC level is below 5 nanograms
correctAnswer: Driving after consuming any cannabis is illegal for all ages
explanation: Driving after consuming any cannabis is illegal for all ages. The guide states there is no safe amount of cannabis for driving.

question: Which of the following is a way cannabis can impair driving?
optionC: Increased drowsiness and loss of motor coordination
correctAnswer: Increased drowsiness and loss of motor coordination
explanation: Cannabis can impair drivers through increased drowsiness, loss of motor coordination, slower reaction times, reduced attention, and inability to judge distances.

question: A driver takes a new prescription medication for the first time. According to the guide, what should they do before driving?
optionA: Wait until they know what effect it has on their judgment, coordination, and reaction time
optionB: Drive only on local roads to test the medication's effect
optionC: Take a lower dose than prescribed when planning to drive
optionD: Drive only during daylight hours for the first week
correctAnswer: Wait until they know what effect it has on their judgment, coordination, and reaction time
explanation: Do not drive if you just started taking prescription drugs for the first time, started a new prescription, or a higher dose. Wait until you know what effect it has on your judgment, coordination, and reaction time.

question: Why might over-the-counter cold or allergy medication be dangerous for drivers?
optionB: They can make a person drowsy, affecting driving ability
correctAnswer: They can make a person drowsy, affecting driving ability
explanation: Over-the-counter drugs taken for headaches, colds, or allergies can make a person drowsy, which could affect driving. Like alcohol, they can affect reflexes, judgment, vision, and alertness.

question: What does the guide say about taking prescription drugs with alcohol?
optionA: It is safe as long as you take half the recommended dose
optionB: It is only dangerous with pain medications
optionC: Prescription drugs cancel out the effects of alcohol
optionD: Many drugs multiply the effects of alcohol and can cause severe impairment
correctAnswer: Many drugs multiply the effects of alcohol and can cause severe impairment
explanation: Some medications might not impact you on their own, but if taken with alcohol, they could cause severe impairment. Many drugs multiply the effects of alcohol or have other side effects.

question: What is polydrug use, and why is it especially dangerous for drivers?
optionA: Using the same drug in increasing amounts; it causes tolerance
optionB: Mixing or taking more than one type of drug; it can produce effects greater than any drug on its own
optionC: Taking drugs at different times of day; it causes unpredictable effects
optionD: Using drugs prescribed for someone else; it causes allergic reactions
correctAnswer: Mixing or taking more than one type of drug; it can produce effects greater than any drug on its own
explanation: Polydrug use is the mixing or taking of more than one type of drug. It can produce effects greater than any drug on its own and is the most common impairment involved in fatal crashes.

question: According to the guide, what is the most common impairment involved in fatal crashes?
optionA: Polydrug use (mixing more than one type of drug)
correctAnswer: Polydrug use (mixing more than one type of drug)
explanation: Polydrug use is the most common impairment involved in fatal crashes. It includes combinations of alcohol, cannabis, illegal drugs, prescription drugs, over-the-counter medicines, and other substances.

question: Which of the following is a sign of driver fatigue that means you should pull over?
optionB: Drifting from your lane and hitting rumble strips
correctAnswer: Drifting from your lane and hitting rumble strips
explanation: Signs of fatigue include drifting from your lane, swerving, tailgating, hitting rumble strips, difficulty focusing, heavy eyelids, and trouble keeping your head up.

question: If you are driving alone and start to feel tired, what does the guide recommend?
optionA: Pull off the road and take a 20-minute nap
optionC: Open the windows and turn up the radio
optionD: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner
correctAnswer: Pull off the road and take a 20-minute nap
explanation: If you're traveling alone and start to feel tired, pull off the road and take a 20-minute nap. It's better to stop and sleep than to risk causing an accident.

question: How often should you plan to stop during long trips to combat fatigue?
correctAnswer: Every 100 miles or 2 hours
explanation: Plan to stop about every 100 miles or 2 hours during long trips. Walk around, get fresh air, and drink water.

question: How many hours of sleep do most people need to stay alert for driving?
correctAnswer: 7 to 9 hours
explanation: Most people need 7 to 9 hours of adequate sleep to stay alert for driving.

question: What does Washington law say about wearing earbuds or headphones while driving?
optionA: It is against the law to wear earbuds, earphones, headphones, or headsets that broadcast sound or cancel noise
optionB: You may wear them only on highways
optionC: You may wear them in both ears if the volume is low
optionD: You may wear them as long as you can still hear sirens
correctAnswer: It is against the law to wear earbuds, earphones, headphones, or headsets that broadcast sound or cancel noise
explanation: It is against the law to drive a vehicle while wearing earbuds, earphones, headphones, or headsets that broadcast sound or cancel noise.

question: Under Washington law, when may a driver use a hands-free device in one ear?
optionA: Any time while driving, regardless of device type
optionB: Only when the device complies with Washington Administrative Code statute 204-10-045
optionD: Only when the vehicle is stopped at a traffic light
correctAnswer: Only when the device complies with Washington Administrative Code statute 204-10-045
explanation: You can use a hands-free device in one ear if it complies with Washington Administrative Code statute 204-10-045.

question: A driver with an instruction permit or intermediate license wants to use a hands-free Bluetooth device while driving. Is this legal in Washington?
optionA: No, they cannot use a cell phone or any mobile electronic device while driving, even if hands-free
optionB: Yes, but only for navigation purposes
optionC: Yes, hands-free devices are permitted for all drivers
optionD: Yes, but only for calls lasting less than 2 minutes
correctAnswer: No, they cannot use a cell phone or any mobile electronic device while driving, even if hands-free
explanation: If you have an instruction permit or intermediate license, you cannot use a cell phone or any mobile electronic device while driving, even if it is hands-free. The only exception is reporting an emergency.

question: Under Washington's distracted driving law, which action is prohibited for ALL drivers regardless of age?
optionB: Holding any electronic device while driving
optionD: Using a mounted GPS for navigation
correctAnswer: Holding any electronic device while driving
explanation: You cannot hold any electronic device while driving (like cell phones, tablets, or gaming devices). This applies to all drivers, regardless of age or experience.

question: Which of the following devices is specifically mentioned as prohibited to hold while driving in Washington?
correctAnswer: Gaming device
explanation: You cannot hold any electronic device while driving, including cell phones, tablets, or gaming devices.

question: What happens to fines for distracted driving after your first violation in Washington?
optionB: They are converted to community service
optionC: They are reduced if you complete a safety course
correctAnswer: They can be doubled
explanation: A law enforcement officer can issue a ticket for violating the distracted driving law, which might result in heavy fines. Fines after your first violation can be doubled.

question: An intermediate license holder receives their second traffic violation. What is the penalty?
optionA: A written warning from the DOL
optionB: License suspended for 6 months or until age 18, whichever comes first
optionD: Required to retake the driving skills test
correctAnswer: License suspended for 6 months or until age 18, whichever comes first
explanation: For an intermediate license holder's second violation, the license is suspended for 6 months or until they turn 18, whichever comes first.

question: Which of the following best describes impaired driving according to the Washington Driver Guide?
optionA: Driving only after consuming illegal drugs
optionB: Driving after consuming more than two alcoholic drinks
optionC: Driving when anything makes it hard to think straight, respond quickly, or control your car
optionD: Driving only when your BAC exceeds the legal limit
correctAnswer: Driving when anything makes it hard to think straight, respond quickly, or control your car
explanation: Impaired driving happens when anything makes it hard for you to think straight, respond quickly, or control your car. This includes alcohol, drugs, or being tired.

question: A driver is parked in a parking lot with the engine running and the keys in the ignition after drinking. Can they be charged with DUI?
optionA: No, because the vehicle is not on a public road
optionB: Yes, because they have the ability to take control of the vehicle's engine or operation
optionC: No, because the vehicle is not moving
optionD: Only if they are in the driver's seat
correctAnswer: Yes, because they have the ability to take control of the vehicle's engine or operation
explanation: DUI applies to being in control of a vehicle, even if it's parked. If you have the ability to take control of a vehicle's engine or operation, you are considered in physical control of the vehicle.

question: According to the guide, which statement about even experienced drivers and alcohol is true?
optionA: Experienced drivers can safely drive after one drink
optionB: Experience helps compensate for alcohol's effects
optionC: Even an experienced driver cannot drive safely after drinking alcohol or using drugs
optionD: Experienced drivers have a higher BAC tolerance
correctAnswer: Even an experienced driver cannot drive safely after drinking alcohol or using drugs
explanation: The guide states that even an experienced driver cannot drive safely after drinking alcohol or using drugs. Making the choice to never drive under the influence will save lives.

question: A medication label warns against 'operating heavy machinery.' According to the guide, what does this include?
correctAnswer: Driving a vehicle
explanation: Warnings against 'operating heavy machinery' include driving a vehicle. Read all warning labels before driving.

question: What is the most common impairing substance involved in impaired driving crashes?
correctAnswer: Alcohol
explanation: Alcohol is the most common impairing substance involved in impaired driving crashes.

question: A 17-year-old intermediate license holder wants to call a friend while driving. Under what circumstance may they use their phone?
optionA: If they use a hands-free Bluetooth device
optionB: If the call lasts less than one minute
optionD: If they pull into a designated phone zone
correctAnswer: Only to report an emergency
explanation: Intermediate license laws restrict the use of cell phones and wireless communication devices while driving, even with hands-free technology. The only exception is using your phone to report an emergency.

question: A driver notices they are blinking frequently, feeling restless, and cannot remember driving the last few miles. What should they do?
optionA: Turn up the air conditioning and continue driving
optionB: Call someone to stay awake while driving
optionC: Pull over and rest because these are signs of fatigue
optionD: Switch to a higher-speed road to stay alert
correctAnswer: Pull over and rest because these are signs of fatigue
explanation: Frequent blinking, feeling restless, and not remembering the last few miles are signs of fatigue. The guide advises pulling over and resting when these signs appear.

question: An octagonal (eight-sided) red sign with white letters means:
optionC: Slow down and watch for hazards
correctAnswer: Stop completely before proceeding
explanation: An octagonal red sign is a stop sign. You must stop at the line, crosswalk, or corner and yield the right-of-way to crossing vehicles and pedestrians.

question: A triangular sign with a red border and white interior means:
optionC: Yield — slow down and allow traffic with the right-of-way to cross first
correctAnswer: Yield — slow down and allow traffic with the right-of-way to cross first
explanation: A yield sign is triangular (point-down) with a red border and white interior. It means you must slow down and allow traffic that has the right-of-way to cross first.

question: What does a diamond-shaped yellow sign indicate?
optionB: A warning about general or unexpected road conditions
correctAnswer: A warning about general or unexpected road conditions
explanation: Diamond-shaped yellow signs are warning signs that alert drivers to general or unexpected road conditions ahead, such as curves, hills, or merging traffic.

question: A pentagon-shaped (five-sided) fluorescent yellow-green sign indicates:
optionB: A school zone or school crossing
correctAnswer: A school zone or school crossing
explanation: Pentagon-shaped fluorescent yellow-green signs warn of school zones, pedestrian areas, and bicycling activity. The color fluorescent yellow-green is specifically reserved for these warnings.

question: A round yellow sign is reserved for warnings about:
correctAnswer: Railroad crossings
explanation: Round yellow signs are advance warning signs for railroad crossings, alerting drivers that tracks are ahead.

question: What color are signs that provide motorist services guidance, such as hospitals and rest areas?
correctAnswer: Blue
explanation: Blue signs provide motorist services guidance, showing the location of hospitals, electric vehicle charging stations, rest areas, and other services.

question: Brown traffic signs are used to identify:
optionA: Motorist services like gas and food
optionB: Public recreation, cultural, and historical areas
correctAnswer: Public recreation, cultural, and historical areas
explanation: Brown signs identify public recreation, cultural, and historical areas such as hiking trails, picnic spaces, national parks, and museums.

question: What color are regulatory signs that tell you about traffic rules such as speed limits?
correctAnswer: White with black text
explanation: White signs are regulatory signs that inform drivers of traffic rules, including speed limits, keep-right requirements, and other mandatory or prohibited actions.

question: Orange signs are used to warn drivers about:
correctAnswer: Construction, maintenance, or emergency operations
explanation: Orange signs warn of construction, maintenance, or emergency operations ahead where workers may be present near the roadway.

question: Green traffic signs are used for:
correctAnswer: Guide or directional information
explanation: Green signs provide guide or directional information, including directions and distances to cities, airports, state lines, and special areas.

question: What does a steady red traffic light mean?
optionA: Stop and wait until the light turns green and the intersection is clear
optionB: Stop and then proceed when safe
optionC: Slow down and prepare to stop
optionD: Yield to traffic already in the intersection
correctAnswer: Stop and wait until the light turns green and the intersection is clear
explanation: A solid red light means stop and wait until the traffic light turns green and there are no vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection before moving ahead.

question: A flashing red traffic light has the same meaning as:
correctAnswer: A stop sign
explanation: A flashing red traffic light functions as a stop sign. You must come to a full stop, and then go when it's your turn.

question: A flashing yellow traffic light has the same meaning as:
correctAnswer: A yield sign
explanation: A flashing yellow light has the same meaning as a yield sign. You should treat the intersection as an uncontrolled intersection and proceed when you have the right-of-way.

question: When a traffic signal is not working (dark or malfunctioning), you should:
optionA: Treat the intersection like a four-way stop
optionC: Yield only to traffic on your left
optionD: Wait for a police officer to direct traffic
correctAnswer: Treat the intersection like a four-way stop
explanation: If a traffic signal isn't working, treat the intersection like a four-way stop. Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic on your right, and proceed cautiously when it's safe.

question: After stopping at a steady red light, when is a right turn permitted?
optionA: Only when a sign says 'right turn allowed on red'
optionB: Only when there is a green right-turn arrow
optionC: Never — you must always wait for a green signal
optionD: When no 'no turn on red' sign is posted and you have plenty of room to enter traffic
correctAnswer: When no 'no turn on red' sign is posted and you have plenty of room to enter traffic
explanation: After coming to a complete stop at a red light, you can turn right if you don't see a 'no turn on red' sign and you have plenty of room to enter traffic.

question: After stopping at a steady red light, a left turn is permitted only onto:
optionA: Any road with a clear gap in traffic
optionB: A one-way street, if no 'no turn on red' sign is posted
optionC: A two-way street when traffic is clear
optionD: A road with a dedicated left-turn lane
correctAnswer: A one-way street, if no 'no turn on red' sign is posted
explanation: After coming to a complete stop at a red light, you can turn left onto a one-way street if you don't see a 'no turn on red' sign and you have plenty of room to enter traffic.

question: A solid yellow traffic light means:
optionA: Speed up to clear the intersection
optionB: Stop immediately regardless of your position
optionC: The light is changing to red — slow down and prepare to stop
correctAnswer: The light is changing to red — slow down and prepare to stop
explanation: A solid yellow light means the light is changing to red. Slow down and prepare to stop. You are not allowed to accelerate beyond the posted speed limit to enter or clear an intersection.

question: What does a yellow arrow signal mean?
optionA: You may turn after yielding to oncoming traffic
optionB: You have a protected turn — proceed without yielding
optionC: The signal is about to turn red — prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic
optionD: Turn is prohibited in the direction of the arrow
correctAnswer: The signal is about to turn red — prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic
explanation: A yellow arrow means the light is going to turn red soon. Prepare to stop and give the right-of-way to oncoming traffic.

question: A green arrow signal means:
optionA: You have the right-of-way to travel in the direction of the arrow with no conflicting traffic
optionB: You may proceed in the direction of the arrow but must yield to oncoming traffic
optionC: You may turn only if the intersection is clear
optionD: Proceed with caution — crossing traffic may still be present
correctAnswer: You have the right-of-way to travel in the direction of the arrow with no conflicting traffic
explanation: A green arrow gives you the right-of-way to travel in that direction. There should be no oncoming vehicles, crossing traffic, or pedestrians while the arrow is green.

question: A red arrow signal means:
optionA: You may turn after stopping and yielding
optionB: Slow down and prepare to stop
optionC: You cannot go in the direction of the arrow
optionD: Yield to oncoming traffic before turning
correctAnswer: You cannot go in the direction of the arrow
explanation: A red arrow means you can't go in the direction of the arrow. You must stop and wait.

question: At a solid green traffic light, a driver turning left must:
optionA: Proceed immediately since green means go
optionB: Honk to alert oncoming traffic of the turn
optionC: Wait for a green arrow before turning
optionD: Yield to approaching vehicles — oncoming traffic has the right-of-way
correctAnswer: Yield to approaching vehicles — oncoming traffic has the right-of-way
explanation: When turning left at a green light, you must yield to approaching vehicles. Oncoming traffic has the right-of-way. Wait for a safe break in traffic before completing the turn.

question: What is true about accelerating through a yellow light?
optionA: It is legal if you can clear the intersection before it turns red
optionB: It is allowed only if no pedestrians are present
optionC: You are not allowed to accelerate beyond the posted speed limit to enter or clear an intersection
optionD: It is permitted on multi-lane roads
correctAnswer: You are not allowed to accelerate beyond the posted speed limit to enter or clear an intersection
explanation: You are not allowed to accelerate beyond the posted speed limit to enter or clear an intersection when the light is yellow.

question: You are already in an intersection when the light turns yellow. You should:
optionB: Back up to the stop line
optionC: Speed up to exit the intersection faster
optionD: Continue through the intersection at the posted speed
correctAnswer: Continue through the intersection at the posted speed
explanation: If you're in the intersection when the yellow light comes on, continue through the intersection at the posted speed. Do not stop in the intersection or accelerate.

question: A 'Do Not Enter' sign is a square sign featuring:
optionA: A white horizontal line inside a red circle
optionB: A red circle with a red slash over a symbol
optionC: A red octagon with white letters
correctAnswer: A white horizontal line inside a red circle
explanation: A Do Not Enter sign is a square sign with a white horizontal line inside a circle, indicating you can't enter the street from that direction.

question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and a red slash over a symbol means:
optionD: Certain actions such as turns or U-turns are not allowed
correctAnswer: Certain actions such as turns or U-turns are not allowed
explanation: Regulatory signs with a red circle and red slash over a symbol indicate that certain actions, such as left turns, right turns, or U-turns, are not allowed.

question: If you see a 'Wrong Way' sign while driving, you should:
optionB: Pull to the right and stop
optionC: Slow down and proceed with caution
optionD: Continue and look for a detour sign
correctAnswer: Stop and turn around immediately
explanation: A Wrong Way sign alerts you that you're driving in the wrong direction and is meant to prevent head-on collisions. You must stop and turn around immediately.

question: What is the posted speed limit in a school zone in Washington?
correctAnswer: 20 mph
explanation: The school zone speed limit is 20 mph because higher speeds increase the risk of fatal crashes near schools.

question: In a work zone, fines for traffic offenses are:
optionB: The same as in other areas
correctAnswer: Doubled when workers are present
explanation: Fines double for offenses committed while driving in construction areas when workers are present.

question: Flashing red lights at a railroad crossing mean:
optionA: Slow down and proceed with caution
optionB: You may proceed if you don't see a train
optionD: A train is approaching — stop and stay outside the gates
correctAnswer: A train is approaching — stop and stay outside the gates
explanation: Flashing red lights at a railroad crossing mean a train is approaching and you need to stay outside of the gates.

question: When lights are flashing and bells are ringing at a railroad crossing, you must stop even if:
optionA: You can see the train is far away
optionB: The gate is not down yet
correctAnswer: The gate is not down yet
explanation: When lights are flashing and bells are ringing at a train crossing, you must stop — whether the gate is down or not. Never drive around the gate.

question: When stopping for a railroad crossing signal, you must stop between what distances from the nearest rail?
correctAnswer: 15 and 50 feet
explanation: You must stop between 15 and 50 feet away from the nearest rail of a crossing when warning signals are active.

question: On a lane-use control signal above a reversible lane, a steady yellow X means:
optionA: The lane is open to traffic in your direction
optionB: The lane is closed — do not enter
optionC: The lane is for emergency vehicles only
optionD: The lane is changing direction — move out as soon as it's safe
correctAnswer: The lane is changing direction — move out as soon as it's safe
explanation: A steady yellow X over a reversible lane means the lane is changing direction, and you should move out of the lane as soon as it's safe.

question: On a lane-use control signal, a red X means:
optionA: The lane is about to change direction
optionB: The lane is reserved for carpools
optionD: Slow down — the lane is merging
correctAnswer: You cannot use this lane
explanation: A red X over a reversible lane means you cannot use that lane. Only a green arrow means the lane is open to travel in your direction.

question: On a lane-use control signal, a green arrow means:
optionA: You can use the lane for travel in your direction
optionB: The lane is about to close
optionC: The lane is reserved for emergency vehicles
optionD: The lane is for high-occupancy vehicles only
correctAnswer: You can use the lane for travel in your direction
explanation: A green arrow over a reversible lane means you can use the lane for travel in your direction.

question: Traffic control devices include signals, signs, and road markings. Who has the authority to overrule these devices?
optionC: Law enforcement, construction workers, maintenance personnel, and school crossing guards
correctAnswer: Law enforcement, construction workers, maintenance personnel, and school crossing guards
explanation: Law enforcement, construction workers, maintenance personnel, and school crossing guards can direct traffic and overrule traffic signals. Their orders or directions must be followed.

question: A 'One Way' sign with an arrow pointing left tells you:
optionB: You must turn left at the next intersection
optionC: The left lane is for turning only
optionD: Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow on that street
correctAnswer: Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow on that street
explanation: One Way signs identify where traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow. You must never drive the wrong way on a one-way street.

question: What does a fluorescent yellow-green colored sign specifically warn about?
correctAnswer: School, pedestrian, and bicycling activity
explanation: Fluorescent yellow-green signs specifically warn of school, pedestrian, and bicycling activity areas.

question: A speed warning sign (often seen before curves) indicates:
optionA: The mandatory minimum speed for that section
optionB: The maximum legal speed limit for that section
optionC: A recommended speed change for a potential hazard
optionD: The speed limit only during wet conditions
correctAnswer: A recommended speed change for a potential hazard
explanation: Speed warning signs indicate that a speed change is recommended for a potential hazard or road condition, often a curve or turn. Adjust your speed appropriately.

question: How does a flashing red light differ from a steady red light at an intersection?
optionA: A flashing red requires you to wait for green; a steady red allows turns
optionB: A flashing red means yield; a steady red means stop
optionC: A flashing red functions as a stop sign (stop then proceed when safe); a steady red requires waiting for green
optionD: There is no difference — both require stopping until the light changes
correctAnswer: A flashing red functions as a stop sign (stop then proceed when safe); a steady red requires waiting for green
explanation: A flashing red functions as a stop sign — stop and proceed when it's your turn. A steady red requires you to stop and wait until the light turns green and the intersection is clear.

question: How does a flashing yellow light differ from a steady yellow light?
optionA: Flashing yellow means yield/proceed with right-of-way; steady yellow means the light is about to turn red
optionB: Flashing yellow means stop; steady yellow means yield
optionC: Both mean the same thing — slow down and prepare to stop
optionD: Flashing yellow means the signal is broken; steady yellow means caution
correctAnswer: Flashing yellow means yield/proceed with right-of-way; steady yellow means the light is about to turn red
explanation: A flashing yellow functions like a yield sign — proceed when you have the right-of-way. A steady yellow means the light is changing to red and you should prepare to stop.

question: You will NOT see a flashing green traffic light in Washington state. Where might you encounter one?
optionA: Oregon, as a pedestrian crossing warning
optionB: California, as a protected turn signal
optionC: Idaho, as a school zone indicator
optionD: British Columbia, Canada, as a warning that pedestrians are waiting to cross
correctAnswer: British Columbia, Canada, as a warning that pedestrians are waiting to cross
explanation: You won't see a flashing green light in Washington state. However, you might see them in British Columbia, Canada, as a warning that pedestrians are waiting to cross.

question: A slow-moving vehicle, such as a farm vehicle designed to go 25 mph or less, is identified by:
optionA: A round orange sign on the front
optionB: A flashing blue light on top
optionC: A triangle sign or emblem on the back
optionD: A rectangular white sign on the side
correctAnswer: A triangle sign or emblem on the back
explanation: Agricultural and farm vehicles designed to go 25 mph or less will have a triangle sign or emblem on the back to alert other drivers.

question: What does a red sign color indicate?
correctAnswer: Prohibitive or restricted action
explanation: Red as a sign color indicates a prohibitive or restricted action, such as stop, yield, do not enter, or wrong way.

question: Automated traffic safety cameras in Washington can record images when you fail to stop at a steady red light, exceed the speed limit in a school zone, or:
optionB: Fail to yield at a yield sign
optionD: Fail to stop at a railroad crossing signal
correctAnswer: Fail to stop at a railroad crossing signal
explanation: Automated cameras record images if you fail to stop at a steady red light, fail to stop at a railroad crossing signal, or exceed the speed limit in a school zone.

question: A sign indicating a shared center lane left turn only means the lane is reserved for:
optionA: Passing slower vehicles from either direction
optionB: Left-turning vehicles traveling in one direction only
optionD: Left-turning vehicles from either direction, not for through traffic or passing
correctAnswer: Left-turning vehicles from either direction, not for through traffic or passing
explanation: A shared center lane left turn only sign indicates the lane is reserved for left-turning vehicles from either direction and is not to be used for through traffic or passing other vehicles.

question: You arrive at a four-way stop at the same time as a vehicle to your right. Neither of you is turning. Who has the right-of-way?
optionA: You, because you are to their left
optionC: The vehicle traveling on the wider street
correctAnswer: The vehicle to your right
explanation: At a four-way stop, if two vehicles arrive at approximately the same time, you must yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: At a four-way stop, three vehicles arrive at approximately the same time. You arrived first, but plan to turn left. The vehicle across from you is going straight. What should you do?
optionA: Go first because you arrived first
optionB: Flash your lights to signal your intent to turn
optionC: Wait, because any vehicle turning left must yield to vehicles going straight
optionD: Turn left quickly before the other vehicle enters the intersection
correctAnswer: Wait, because any vehicle turning left must yield to vehicles going straight
explanation: At a four-way stop, any vehicle turning left must yield the right-of-way to vehicles going straight or turning right, regardless of arrival order.

question: At a two-way stop intersection, you are on the stopped road and want to turn left. A vehicle on the through road is approaching from your left. Who has the right-of-way?
optionA: The vehicle on the through road going straight
optionB: You, because the other vehicle is to your left
optionC: Whoever reaches the center of the intersection first
correctAnswer: The vehicle on the through road going straight
explanation: At a two-way stop, turning vehicles must yield to the vehicle going straight. The vehicle going straight has the right-of-way.

question: When making either a left or right turn at an intersection, Washington law requires you to turn into which lane?
optionA: Any available lane on the new road
optionB: The lane closest to the direction you are coming from
optionD: The far lane to avoid other turning traffic
correctAnswer: The lane closest to the direction you are coming from
explanation: State law requires you to turn into the lane closest to the direction you are coming from. Once you complete your turn, you can change to another lane if needed.

question: How far before a turn must you activate your turn signal?
correctAnswer: 100 feet
explanation: You must put on your turn signal at least 100 feet before you turn left or right across oncoming traffic.

question: You are waiting to turn left at a green light. Oncoming traffic is approaching. What should you do?
optionA: Yield to oncoming traffic and wait for a safe gap before turning
optionB: Turn quickly before the oncoming vehicles arrive
optionC: Honk to alert oncoming traffic of your turn
optionD: Proceed because a green light always gives you the right-of-way
correctAnswer: Yield to oncoming traffic and wait for a safe gap before turning
explanation: When turning left at a green light, you must yield to approaching vehicles. Oncoming traffic has the right-of-way. Wait for a break in traffic before completing your turn.

question: In Washington, when are U-turns NOT allowed?
optionB: At any intersection controlled by traffic lights
optionD: Where a sign prohibits them, on a curve, or near the crest of a hill
correctAnswer: Where a sign prohibits them, on a curve, or near the crest of a hill
explanation: In Washington, U-turns are generally allowed unless a sign is posted telling you they are not allowed. You must also not make a U-turn on a curve or when approaching the crest of a hill because you need clear visibility in all directions.

question: You approach a T-intersection where the road you are on ends at a through road. There is a yield sign. Who has the right-of-way?
optionA: You, because you are making a turn
optionD: The vehicle to your right only
correctAnswer: Traffic on the through road
explanation: At a T-intersection, passing traffic on the through road has the right-of-way. Yield or stop signs let you know this.

question: When approaching a roundabout, you must yield to:
optionD: All traffic already in the roundabout
correctAnswer: All traffic already in the roundabout
explanation: You must look left and yield to all traffic already in the roundabout since they have the right-of-way. Enter only when you see a gap in traffic.

question: What is the correct direction of travel inside a roundabout?
optionC: Either direction depending on your exit
correctAnswer: Counterclockwise
explanation: In a roundabout, all traffic enters to the right and travels counterclockwise around the raised center island.

question: You are driving through a roundabout when you hear an emergency vehicle siren behind you. What should you do?
optionB: Drive through the roundabout, exit, and then pull over
optionC: Speed up to exit the roundabout faster
optionD: Cut across the center island to get out of the way
correctAnswer: Drive through the roundabout, exit, and then pull over
explanation: If an emergency vehicle approaches while you are in a roundabout, drive through the roundabout and pull over after exiting, just like you would at any other intersection.

question: Roundabouts are designed for travel at what speed range?
correctAnswer: 15 to 25 mph
explanation: Roundabouts are designed for speeds between 15 and 25 mph. Slow down when approaching a roundabout.

question: After coming to a complete stop at a red light, you may turn left onto:
optionA: Any street, as long as there is no oncoming traffic
optionB: A two-way street, as long as you yield
optionC: A one-way street only if a green arrow appears
optionD: A one-way street, if no 'no turn on red' sign is posted
correctAnswer: A one-way street, if no 'no turn on red' sign is posted
explanation: After coming to a complete stop at a red light, you can turn left onto a one-way street if you don't see a 'no turn on red' sign and you have plenty of room to enter traffic.

question: You approach an intersection with no traffic signs or signals. A vehicle is already in the intersection. What must you do?
optionA: Enter the intersection and yield once inside
optionB: Proceed if you are on the wider road
optionC: Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle already in the intersection
optionD: Honk to signal your approach and proceed
correctAnswer: Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle already in the intersection
explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, you must yield the right-of-way if a vehicle is already in the intersection.

question: You are entering a paved state highway from an unpaved road. Who has the right-of-way?
optionA: Traffic on the paved state highway
optionB: You, if there is no stop sign
correctAnswer: Traffic on the paved state highway
explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, you must yield if you enter a paved road from an unpaved road, or if you enter or cross a state highway from a secondary road.

question: How far are you allowed to travel in a two-way left turn lane?
correctAnswer: 300 feet
explanation: You should not travel farther than 300 feet in a center two-way left turn lane. These lanes are reserved for vehicles making left turns or U-turns.

question: A two-way left turn lane in the center of a road may be used for:
optionB: Making left turns from either direction or permitted U-turns
optionD: Merging onto the road from a side street
correctAnswer: Making left turns from either direction or permitted U-turns
explanation: Shared center lanes are reserved for vehicles making left turns in either direction from or into the roadway, or U-turns when permitted. They must not be used for passing.

question: You hear a siren and see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you. What must you do?
optionA: Speed up to get out of the way
optionC: Move to the left lane and slow down
optionD: Pull to the right side of the road and stop
correctAnswer: Pull to the right side of the road and stop
explanation: When you see or hear emergency vehicle signals, immediately pull your vehicle to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until the emergency vehicle has passed before reentering traffic.

question: Every intersection in Washington is legally considered a:
correctAnswer: Crosswalk, whether marked or unmarked
explanation: Every intersection is legally defined as a crosswalk regardless of whether a crosswalk marking is present. You must yield to pedestrians.

question: You are at a four-way stop. You arrived second after the vehicle across from you. A third vehicle arrives to your right. In what order should vehicles proceed?
optionA: You, the vehicle across, then the vehicle to your right
optionB: The vehicle to your right, then you, then the vehicle across
optionC: The vehicle across from you first, then you, then the third vehicle
correctAnswer: The vehicle across from you first, then you, then the third vehicle
explanation: At a four-way stop, the first vehicle to arrive goes first, the second goes second, and so on. The vehicle across arrived first and goes first, you go second, and the third vehicle goes last.

question: You stop at a stop sign but cannot see cross traffic because a parked vehicle is blocking your view. What should you do?
optionA: Honk your horn and proceed quickly
optionB: Wait until the parked vehicle moves
optionC: Back up and try a different route
optionD: Edge forward slowly until you can see, which also lets crossing drivers see your front
correctAnswer: Edge forward slowly until you can see, which also lets crossing drivers see your front
explanation: If you stop on the stop line but your view is blocked, edge forward slowly until you can see. This allows crossing drivers to see the front of your vehicle and gives them a chance to slow down.

question: Before entering an intersection, you must make sure there is enough space for you to:
optionA: Cross or turn without blocking the intersection
optionC: Make a complete stop inside the intersection if needed
correctAnswer: Cross or turn without blocking the intersection
explanation: Before entering an intersection, make sure there is enough space for you to cross or turn without blocking the intersection.

question: You are approaching a roundabout and want to turn left. Which lane should you use?
optionC: The lane indicated by the lane choice sign for left turns
correctAnswer: The lane indicated by the lane choice sign for left turns
explanation: The lane choice sign at a roundabout shows which lanes are used for right turns, straight through travel, and left turns. Pick the correct lane as you approach and stay in it until you exit.

question: When exiting a roundabout, you must stop for:
optionB: Vehicles behind you in the roundabout
optionC: Vehicles waiting to enter the roundabout
optionD: No one, because vehicles in the roundabout always have the right-of-way
correctAnswer: Pedestrians and bicyclists in crosswalks
explanation: You must stop for pedestrians and bicyclists in crosswalks both when you enter and when you exit the roundabout.

question: A traffic signal is completely dark and not working at all. How should you treat the intersection?
correctAnswer: As a four-way stop
explanation: If a traffic signal isn't working, treat the intersection like a four-way stop. Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic on your right, and proceed cautiously when safe.

question: At a Y-intersection, a minor road connects with a major road. There is a stop sign where the minor road meets the major road. Who has the right-of-way?
optionB: The vehicle on the minor road if it stopped first
correctAnswer: Vehicles on the major road
explanation: At a Y-intersection, the cars on major roads have the right-of-way. There may be a stop sign where the minor road connects with the major road.

question: You are turning right at an intersection and a bicyclist is riding behind you approaching the same intersection. What should you do before turning?
optionA: Speed up to complete your turn before the bicyclist arrives
optionB: Check behind you and yield to the bicyclist before making your turn
optionD: The bicyclist must always yield to turning vehicles
correctAnswer: Check behind you and yield to the bicyclist before making your turn
explanation: Check behind you for bicyclists and yield to them before making your turn. Bicyclists might be moving toward you faster than you realize.

question: At a four-way stop, two vehicles arrive at the same time. One is turning left, the other is going straight. Who goes first?
optionA: The vehicle turning left because left turns take longer
optionC: It depends on which vehicle is to the right
correctAnswer: The vehicle going straight
explanation: At a four-way stop, any vehicle turning left must yield the right-of-way to vehicles going straight or turning right.

question: When a pedestrian is crossing in a crosswalk, when may you proceed?
optionA: As soon as the pedestrian passes your lane
optionB: After the pedestrian has cleared your lane and one additional lane
optionC: Only after the pedestrian has completely crossed the street
optionD: Immediately, if you can steer around the pedestrian
correctAnswer: After the pedestrian has cleared your lane and one additional lane
explanation: You must wait until a pedestrian has cleared your lane and one additional lane before proceeding through a crosswalk.

question: A flashing yellow traffic light means you should:
optionA: Stop completely and wait for it to change
optionB: Treat the intersection as uncontrolled and proceed when you have the right-of-way
optionC: Speed up to clear the intersection
correctAnswer: Treat the intersection as uncontrolled and proceed when you have the right-of-way
explanation: A flashing yellow light has the same meaning as a yield sign. Treat the intersection as an uncontrolled intersection and proceed when you have the right-of-way.

question: You are on a secondary road approaching an uncontrolled intersection with a state highway. Who must yield?
correctAnswer: You, on the secondary road
explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, you must yield the right-of-way if you enter or cross a state highway from a secondary road.

question: You are in a multi-lane roundabout in the inner lane. A large truck is also in the roundabout. What should you be aware of?
optionA: Trucks must exit the roundabout first
optionB: Trucks are not allowed in roundabouts
optionC: Trucks are allowed to use both lanes and cross the truck apron
optionD: Trucks must always stay in the outer lane
correctAnswer: Trucks are allowed to use both lanes and cross the truck apron
explanation: Large vehicles are allowed to cross truck aprons and both lanes as they approach and drive through the roundabout. Give large vehicles plenty of space.

question: Pedestrians are crossing at an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection. What must you do?
optionA: Honk to warn them they are not in a marked crosswalk
optionC: Yield only if a crossing guard is present
optionD: Yield to them because every intersection is legally a crosswalk
correctAnswer: Yield to them because every intersection is legally a crosswalk
explanation: Every intersection is legally a crosswalk, whether marked or unmarked. You must yield to pedestrians in any crosswalk.

question: After an emergency vehicle with flashing lights passes you, when may you reenter traffic?
optionC: After signaling and when the emergency vehicle has passed and it is safe
optionD: Only when a police officer directs you
correctAnswer: After signaling and when the emergency vehicle has passed and it is safe
explanation: Wait until the emergency vehicle has passed before signaling and reentering traffic. You should reenter traffic in the order you were traveling before.

question: You are turning right on a red light. A pedestrian has started crossing the street you want to turn onto. What must you do?
optionA: Yield to the pedestrian and wait until they clear your path
optionB: Honk and proceed, since you already made a complete stop
optionC: Complete your turn behind the pedestrian
optionD: Turn into the far lane to avoid the pedestrian
correctAnswer: Yield to the pedestrian and wait until they clear your path
explanation: You must yield to pedestrians in any crosswalk. Even when turning right on red after a complete stop, you must wait until pedestrians have cleared your path before proceeding.

question: You are making a right turn from a two-lane road onto another road. Into which lane must you turn?
optionA: The leftmost lane of the new road
optionD: The rightmost lane (closest to the direction you are coming from)
correctAnswer: The rightmost lane (closest to the direction you are coming from)
explanation: State law requires you to turn into the lane closest to the direction you are coming from. For a right turn, this is the rightmost lane of the new road.

question: You are in a designated turn lane at a major intersection. After entering the lane, you decide you no longer want to turn. What must you do?
optionA: Change back to a through lane before the intersection
optionC: Stop and wait for the next green light to go straight
optionD: Back up to exit the turn lane
correctAnswer: Follow through with the turn
explanation: Once you're in a turn lane, you must follow through with the turn.

question: At an uncontrolled intersection, you plan to make a left turn. A vehicle is approaching from the opposite direction going straight. Who must yield?
optionA: The approaching vehicle because you are already turning
optionB: Neither vehicle needs to yield at an uncontrolled intersection
optionC: You must yield because you plan to turn left
optionD: The vehicle traveling at a slower speed
correctAnswer: You must yield because you plan to turn left
explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, you must yield the right-of-way if you plan to make a left turn and a vehicle is approaching from the opposite direction.

question: A traffic calming circle requires you to travel in which direction around the center island?
correctAnswer: Counterclockwise
explanation: A traffic calming circle is an intersection with a center island that traffic flows counterclockwise around. The same right-of-way rules apply as at any other intersection.

question: You approach a mid-block crosswalk where a pedestrian is waiting to cross. There is no stop sign. What must you do?
optionA: Slow down but continue if the pedestrian has not yet stepped off the curb
optionB: Stop to allow the pedestrian to cross
optionC: Proceed because there is no stop sign
optionD: Honk to alert the pedestrian and continue
correctAnswer: Stop to allow the pedestrian to cross
explanation: Pedestrians always have the right-of-way in a marked crosswalk. Drivers should stop to allow pedestrians and bicyclists to cross, regardless of whether the crosswalk has a stop sign.

question: When must you yield to pedestrians?
optionA: Only at marked crosswalks with signals
optionB: Only when they are in a school zone
optionC: Only when they have a walk signal
correctAnswer: Always
explanation: Washington law requires drivers to always yield to pedestrians. Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crosswalks and intersections whether marked or not.

question: When may you proceed after stopping for a pedestrian in a crosswalk?
optionA: After the pedestrian has cleared your lane and one additional lane
optionB: As soon as the pedestrian passes your lane
optionC: After the pedestrian reaches the opposite curb
correctAnswer: After the pedestrian has cleared your lane and one additional lane
